rv.q: Less convincing are the surveillance-state cameras, first overseeing the barn and later forming the features of a human puppet.
It is an engaging and well-pitched production; only the largely dialogue-free scenes, in which the animals rise up against their human oppressors, achieve less narrative clarity.
I really enjoyed both plays and I would award them both a five-star rating.
Nonetheless, this production has much to commend it.
This adaptation does justice to Orwell's powerful message, delivering a production that is both entertaining and intellectually stimulating.
This is a thought-provoking chilling production; it pulls no punches and is not always an easy watch but it is still so relevant to today's world.

cn.t: This visceral, physically intense adaptation of Orwell's classic proves timeless and relevant, though critical reception ranges from enthusiastic praise for its unsettling intimacy to more reserved assessments of its execution.
